messages:
Nina - Support: FYI OlivePool is seeing sustained 429s from their dedicated pool during yesterday's campaign. Customer reports high token-per-second errors and tail latencies. Attached logs show admission rejects with `insufficient_burst_headroom`. Can eng take a look?

Alex - EngSRE: Thanks, looped in. Do we have pool id + recent admission logs? also want to know if autoscaler bounced nodes during the spike.

Nina - Support: Pool: dp-olive-12, customer account olivepool-prod. I grabbed a short snippet from the admission controller at 2024-04-15T22:14Z: ```[2024-04-15T22:14:02Z] admission:acct=olivepool-prod pool=dp-olive-12 req_id=abc123 token_rate=9500 headroom_left=120 burst_credits=0 action=reject reason=insufficient_burst_headroom``` They say average request token size jumped from ~60 to ~600 for the campaign.

Josh - EngRuntime: That token size change matters a lot — our admission is token-based. If average tokens/request jumps 10x the burst credits will be consumed fast. Can you also pull proxy metrics for request_count vs tokens_emitted?

Priya - EngPlatform: I'm checking autoscaler logs. Initial scale triggered at 22:10, added 2 workers, but scale stabilization window prevented additional scale until ~22:18. There was a cooldown that prevented immediate extra capacity.

Alex - EngSRE: Looks like a classic staircase load pattern: big initial spike of long requests exhausted burst credits, admission started rejecting, then clients retried and amplified the pressure. Two quick asks: (1) repro steps we can run in staging to emulate token-heavy burst, (2) short mitigation to restore customer service now.

Nina - Support: OlivePool is ok with a temporary capacity bump for 1 hour. They can also route to hosted fallback if we ask them.

Sam - Account: Customer prefers temporary bump on Dedicated over routing to hosted due to data controls. Please confirm ETA and cost implications.

Josh - EngRuntime: Mitigation plan: (A) immediate: apply emergency override to admission to grant +30k burst credits to dp-olive-12 and reduce token_cost multiplier for 10 minutes; (B) short term: increase autoscaler aggressiveness for that pool (lower stabilization window + faster scale-up); (C) long term: recommend per-customer token smoothing + prewarm for campaigns. I'm ready to patch if EngSRE approves.

Alex - EngSRE: Approve (A) and (B) for emergency. Josh please run the override and post the command you run. Priya, coordinate autoscaler change and watch for overshoot.

ops-bot: deploy requested by Josh - EngRuntime for override `admission.override --pool dp-olive-12 --burst+30000 --ttl 600 --reason "customer emergency"` queued on canary.

Josh - EngRuntime: Ran the override, canary passed. Command: ```./infractl admission override --pool dp-olive-12 --burst-add 30000 --ttl 600 --reason "olive campaign emergency"``` Response from control plane: `override_applied id=ovr-879 status=active expires=2024-04-15T22:24:02Z`.

Alex - EngSRE: Seeing immediate reduction in 429s in the proxy metrics and burst_credits metric now shows +29k. Latency tail still elevated but declining. Good sign.

Priya - EngPlatform: Autoscaler tweak deployed: reduced stabilization_window from 120s->30s for dp-olive-12 and decreased cpu/tps scale thresholds to be more aggressive for active campaigns. Monitor for flapping.

Nina - Support: Customer reports decreased 429s and their engineers say the campaign is progressing. They still see some 500s from model container OOMs though.

Josh - EngRuntime: Model container OOMs probably due to longer sequences + KV cache size increase. Rolling a config change to increase container memory allocation for that pool by +15%. Command: ```kubectl patch deployment dp-olive-12-runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"6Gi"}}}]}}}}'```

ops-bot: patch applied to dp-olive-12-runtime, rollout started.

Alex - EngSRE: Monitoring: error rate dropped from 18%->2% over 8 minutes, 95th latency down from 1.4s->620ms. Will keep open until stable for 30m.

Priya - EngPlatform: NOTE for postmortem: autoscaler cooldown/stabilization was primary contributor — policy assumed uniform token sizes. We should add a campaign-mode flag that temporarily relaxes cooldowns if a pool sees sustained token_size > threshold.

Sam - Account: Customer thanks the team and accepts the temporary bump; please follow up with a recommended long-term config and run cost estimate.

Nina - Support: Next steps assigned: Alex will own postmortem and remediation doc, Josh owns runtime memory/runtime admission tuning, Priya will propose autoscaler campaign-mode. I'll follow up with customer and schedule a quick runbook review.

Alex - EngSRE: Quick repro in staging for devs: simulate 1k rps with `tok=600` payload using the load harness: ```python load_gen.py --target-host dp-olive-12.proxy.redwood.local --rps 1000 --duration 60 --avg_tokens 600``` That should exhaust burst credits and reproduce staircase rejection pattern.

Josh - EngRuntime: Added a short-term admission heuristic to avoid rejecting if burst_credits==0 but pool_util < 60% and average_latency < 700ms — prevents premature rejects during warmups. Deployed as feature-flag `admission.relax_warmup` on dp-olive-12.

Alex - EngSRE: Flag acknowledged. Make sure we have metrics to revert if it causes token oversubscription.

Nina - Support: Closing note: Customer will send campaign schedule next week so we can prewarm and avoid surprises. Thanks everyone. :tada:
